What is the worst way of getting rejected for a job?

Over the past few months, I was on an intense job search journey, targeting some of the best in the industry.

I put my best foot forward with:

AMAZON: 3 interview emails, ultimately failing in the second technical round.

GOOGLE: Completed initial assessment. Still waiting on feedback, but moving on.

MakeMyTrip (MMT): This one was a rollercoaster. I aced the assessment and received an email saying I was among the top shortlisted candidates, only to get rejected in the next paragraph.

A humbling reminder of how razor-thin the margins are at this level.

IBM, Flipkart and others: Assessed/interviewed, didn’t hear back.

Has anyone else experienced the whiplash of a compliment followed by a rejection in the same email?

Okay, so the second piece of the missing puzzle is 'The reason behind building LSTMs.'

I searched for the original LSTM research paper and realized what they were actually built for.

The paper 'LSTM can Solve Hard Long Time Lag Problems' answered many questions for me.

This experience taught me something important:

Never blindly trust tutorials.
Always ask questions and do your own digging.

Reading research papers provides a depth of understanding that short-form explanations often miss.

HOW BRUSHING MY TEETH UNLOCKED LSTMs

When I started exploring machine learning and NLP, I struggled to understand why LSTMs actually worked.

Most tutorials explained the architecture but never the thought process behind it.

Then one day while brushing my teeth, I realized the missing piece:

VECTORS.

Once I started thinking in terms of vector algebra instead of raw numbers, things finally clicked.

Sometimes understanding comes from the weirdest moments.

FOUR YEARS OF PYTHON AND I JUST LEARNED THIS!!

Recently, I discovered something interesting while solving a Python problem.

Modifying a global list inside a function behaves differently from modifying a global variable.

Example:

flag = False
glaf = [False]

def func():
    flag = True
    glaf[0] = True

Output:
False True

Python still surprises me even after years of coding.

Here is a simple implementation of an ANN (Artificial Neural Network) using a Customer Churn dataset.

The ANN contains:
- one input layer
- two hidden layers

My first Machine Learning project: Ahmedabad House Rent Price Prediction.

This project predicts house rent prices based on locality, BHK count, layout type and furnishing.

Libraries used:
- Pandas
- Matplotlib
- Seaborn
- Scikit-learn

Used K-Fold Cross Validation and GridSearchCV for model evaluation and selection.
